analysis:
Reviewed the BASE text of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (lines 1-1023) against the complete patch. The head side has two changes. First, head lines 221-224 add the actor state `operatorModelFilter: Set<String>?`. Second, head lines 946-948 set it in init: it is nil when backend.enabledModels is empty; otherwise it is the set of enabledModels unioned with config.models ids.

This is operator-local model selection state. It governs which coordinator-pushed models the provider serves, through `operatorFilterAllows`; that consumer is not in this batch. No crypto, attestation, keys (A-003), App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-052..T-058), cache scope (T-041) or add-on hold (TB-012) logic changes here. The operator is already the trusted owner of local configuration (TB-003), so letting the operator restrict models is not a new adversary capability.

Integration questions for other batches:
(1) Does `operatorFilterAllows` treat nil as allow-all, as documented? Would an empty-but-non-nil set block everything (an availability concern only)?
(2) Is the filter only a further restriction applied on top of the existing gates, not a bypass of them? The existing gates are EngineV2SupportedModels, the admitsModel and runtime-eligibility checks (base 942-977), weight-hash verification, and the failedSelfTestHashes/retiringModels tombstones (base 422-430).
(3) The union with config.models lets start-selected models pass even when they are absent from enabled_models; confirm this is intended.
(4) Do live switches update the filter consistently, and do the desired_models/prefetch reconcile paths honor it without re-advertising unverified builds (T-012/T-027)?

No regression was identified in the supplied lines.
